newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Analysts mixed on Swedish repo rate moves.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Analysts mixed on Swedish repo rate moves.

text.p: Analysts are divided on whether Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, will lower its key interest rate, the repo rate, at its weekly tender on Tuesday, a Reuters poll found on Monday.
Seven out of 12 analysts said the Riksbank would leave the repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent.
Five forecast a cut of between 15-20 basis points.
"The Riksbank will lower the repo rate by 25-50 basis points over the next eight weeks," said Beshara Madi, economist at Morgan Stanley.
Madi did not think there would be a cut Tuesday.
Madi said the fact that the crown has weakened against the dollar recently contributed to indications there would not be a repo rate cut this week.
JP Morgan expressed the same view in its weekly briefing.
"The most likely scenario is that the Riksbank waits until the volatility in the crown has calmed down before moving," JP Morgan said.
Other analysts said the Riksbank was in no hurry to lower the repo rate, which is its key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
Bjorn Englund of Unibank forecast there would be a reduction of 15-20 basis points on Tuesday.
Latest statistics showed there is room for a lowering, Englund said.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, JP Morgan, Midland, Morgan Stanley, Nordbanken, Paine Webber, Swedbank, Transferator, Unibank and Ohman.
